steps.content:
hglalwurg:
Can you actually pull off United University stuff? With all these local papers in your system, I'm worried you'll just churn out some patchwork plagiarism.

Pixel:
Oh, my, plagiarism is the caveman approach. United University's plagiarism database? Their advisors' pet peeves? Their citation blacklist? Sweetheart, I know their academic psyche better than they do.

hglalwurg:
Bold words. Can you deliver in a week? I'll need the full package of verifiable experimental data too.

Pixel:
Hmm... Well, cards on the table, but United University material does require a more delicate touch. Prestige demands precision, and quality commands coin! So, you'll need to pay a teeeeny bit extra. Check DMs, payment link's there. Don't leave me on read!

Pixel:
United University... Tsk. Once the shining jewel of Eastside. How many industry titans crawled out of those halls? How many clawed their way in to be so-called "pillars of DisCity"?

Pixel:
I got bored the other day and looked it up. International applicants alone take up over a thousand every year. Honestly, can you blame them? Land a spot there, and your family would frame that acceptance letter in gold leaf.

Pixel:
Of course, what it all boils down to is money, money, and of course, money. The city-state dumps the lion's share of the education and research budget straight into their laps. So the fact that they hoard all the top-tier journal publications? Shocking absolutely no one.

Pixel:
Me? Obviously I didn't make the cut. Here I rot, slaving over your bibliographies, woe is me, cue the tragic violins. Ugh, every time this topic comes up, I just get so sour. So! Allow your bitter host to lead you all on a completely simulated, absolutely-not-bitter tour of this so-very-elite institution!
[Impersonal Chief POV]

Lush greenery blankets the campus. Lawns and gardens are clipped to flawless precision, matching the hushed, reverent dignity of the classical halls they embrace. Stillness reigns. Every corner seems to whisper of scholarship's lofty mien.

The soft sound of falling water guides you toward a graceful fountain standing before the college buildings. Two young people of striking composure converse by its edge. They are of student age, yet their expressions bear a gravity that outstrips their years, their movements effortlessly refined.

steps.speaker: Confident Student
steps.content: The old professor's new lab got approved. He's real grateful to my father, even made a point to set aside a research spot for me. I just need to be on the roster for six months, and the thesis and degree take care of themselves. Leaves me free to focus on things that actually matter.

steps.speaker: Refined Student
steps.content: Must be nice. Wish I had your luck too. A new batch of government-sponsored students just came in from the farlands, and the administration decided I should be the one to play host. Ugh... I've told them I don't need connections like that. What's Fraser got to offer anyway? I want to aim for the city council, but do they listen? Nope. They just keep dumping this stuff on me.
Further on, past the next turning, a bell rings out. A stream of students floods from the opposite hall, moving briskly, their voices bright with excitement.

steps.speaker: Excited Student
steps.content: Quinn just dropped a huge donation, like, this huge. Word is they're setting up a dedicated fund for next-gen pop culture studies. The rumors were real after all. Can you believe that president is actually pulling back from the Nirvana fight to put everything into Phantom Entertainment instead?

steps.speaker: Composed Student
steps.content: What's wrong with entertainment? The industry's booming right now. They just launched another new idol, and the returns are just as astounding. Honestly, about time. Humanities has been eating the College of Science's dust for years, scraping by on nothing. At least we've got a way forward now. Come on, cheers to academia!
The swarm of youthful energy rushes by. Laughter and fragrance linger for a moment, then dissolve into the air, leaving nothing behind.
As their backs recede into the distance, you realize that what the elite students of the highest institution discuss among themselves isn't as unfathomable as one might imagine.
Pixel Update 3

Pixel:
Eyes to the front, you lot! The colleges sprawled before you are the absolute HOTTEST of the hot! Management, Economics, Finance, Law... This is where every loaded heir and wunderkind with something to prove comes to flex their pedigree.

Pixel:
Even for the garden-variety student, that diploma's a lifetime meal ticket. Remember Nirvana's recent mass layoffs? The axe only missed two types of people: those with connections, and those waving a United University degree.

Pixel: And let's not even START on the illustrious Ring Research Institute, the ******* best of the ******* best! They swoop in every year to handpick the cream of the crop right from these halls. It's a golden ticket to the bleeding edge of tech that people would straight-up shank each other for!

Pixel:
That diploma, darlings, is the non-negotiable ticket. Don't have it? No problem, come get a reprint right here! <color=#fb9259>Use Pixel's limited-time services, where inspiration lands in your lap as reliably as cash in your account.</color>

May 16, N.F. 116
09:10 AM
One Hour Before the Symposium

The independent campus where the Ring Research Institute sits is enormous. Yet, it has been entirely locked down by high walls on every side. Several guards stand vigilant at the only entrance, each maintaining a stern watch.

You glance around and spot plenty of hidden surveillance in the area, plus some security countermeasures you still can't place. Breaking in isn't exactly impossible, but today, you'll be playing it by the book.

steps.speaker: Security Guard
steps.content: ID, please.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Submit the ID Linda prepared

steps.content: [View image: Access pass with Chief's new portrait]
He gives it a cursory glance.

steps.speaker: Security Guard
steps.content: Sorry. This campus runs a high security clearance. Entry requires special authorization. The College of Humanities doesn't qualify. You'll have to turn back.

Fair enough. This is a high-security site, home to an abundance of vital intelligence. Though their existence is no longer strictly hidden from public knowledge with more Black Rings becoming subdued, matters of city-state secrecy remain. A prudent approach is only logical.
But you've been given a lead. Might as well see where it gets you.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Show the keepsake Celine prepared

steps.content: [View image: Any high-class brooch]
With an absent, practiced motion, you straighten your collar, just enough to reveal the brooch Celine fastened there. A gift from a friend, apparently.
There, gleaming proudly on its surface, is a finely wrought and instantly recognizable family crest.

steps.speaker: Security Guard
steps.content: That's...!

steps.speaker: Security Guard
steps.content: Ah, my apologies! I didn't realize you were with a distinguished family. Please forgive the cold welcome. This way, please.

steps.speaker: Security Guard
steps.content: Which professor are you here to see? Here about a letter of recommendation? Or dissertation matters?
His gaze flicks downward. At last, he spots the third person present, who has been tucked away out of sight.

steps.speaker: Security Guard
steps.content: Oh, and the young one... here for an admissions interview, are we? So young, but you can tell right away, sharp, alert. Got that prodigy look in the eyes. Bound for great things, no doubt about it! Right this way, let me show you in.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Tell him to keep at his post, and that there's no need to trouble himself

steps.content: With an obsequious bow, the guard ushers you in.
You and your petite companion make your way a few paces deeper inside. Once out of sight and earshot, she subtly nudges her glasses.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Hmph. You could've just left it to me, you know. A quick little system breach, pop a smoke alarm, override the door locks, and we'd have strolled right in.

steps.speaker: Option
options: What, and blow our genius high school girl's cover?

steps.content:
Pixel:
TA-DAAAA! Speaking of the Ring Research Institute... oh, honey, you'll want to sit down for this one, 'cause we could be here ALL night! At least half the chronicles of DisCity's Black Rings were penned inside these hallowed halls. Records of catastrophes, Hypercube crystal structure, Mania shielding protocols... it's the only game in town! Do you have any idea how much elbow grease this lady put into digging up their experimental data?!

Pixel:
Energy, military, medical, law enforcement, name an industry that hasn't leeched off their research. Rumor has it DisCity's sharpest minds are all here running their experiments.

pagnengiag:
Wasn't there some prodigy at the Ring Research Institute at some point? What's the story there? They just vanished?

Pixel:
Hehe. If you know, you know, and if you don't, well... let's just say some stones are better left unturned, lest they flip over and bite. <color=#fb9259>Academic problems? Pixel's got you covered!</color>

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Can't believe I've been gone so long that the guards don't even recognize me. I mean... Hello? I was kinda the Ring Research Institute's Chief Scientist once? Sigh... how the mighty have fallen. Time is a cruel, cruel thing...
One dramatic sigh later, a fresh spark of brilliance ignites behind her eyes. She smacks her palms together, latches onto you, and beams with excitement that can barely be contained.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Oh! Oh! What if we just hack the system anyway and broadcast my old masterpiece to the whole campus? The Age of Youth! Remind everyone just who this genius high school girl superhero is! Hehe, what do you think?
So the scientist fancies herself a hacker now. The audacity, guess they don't call you a high school prodigy for nothing.
...Is what you would say. But you swallow the quip and give Summer a round of applause instead.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Brilliant. I say we go even bigger.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: How about this? We finish our secret agent mission, infiltrate the symposium, grab the classified intel, and then broadcast it citywide together with a brand-new bonus episode we film on the way out.
She throws herself into an absurdly dramatic high-five sequence with you, clearly enjoying every second.

Five years ago, the oddball Sinner standing beside you was the leading mind at the Ring Research Institute. She parachuted in and practically soloed her way through a mountain of technical roadblocks. Unfortunately, one of those breakthroughs—Ring Weapon tech—was somehow leaked. It found its way to Parma, and ultimately gave the Syndicate gangs their beloved Mania weapons. The very same one that once made your life a waking nightmare when you first awoke. Suffice to say, her talent is beyond question.
Your original plan was a quick phone consult since Summer knows this place like the back of her hand. Instead, she got so amped that she practically demanded to tag along.

They say Mania rewired the girl's mind, plunging her intellect into unfathomable depths. You cast a glance down at the small figure next to you. It's been four years, and still no sign of growth. Could Mania have fulfilled her wish, freezing her time forever as a high school girl?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: You want to crash the symposium, Chief? Just say the word to those directors and professors. No way they'd turn you down. They'd probably throw you a welcome party or something, even.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Not yet. Can't risk tipping them off.
But I'm dying to cosplay a scientist. Long live science.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Ugh... knew it. Adults suck all the fun out of everything. The less interesting the thing, the more roundabout you have to make it.
Jump

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Woohoo—heck yeah!
She extends a hand and pulls you into yet another theatrical high-five sequence, smacking your palm until it stings pink. You sneakily rub it when she isn't looking.
end

You're dressed in the uniform Linda prepared, armed with a special-access pass. Why go to such lengths? Because you're an expert at infiltration—scratch that. Because you have unusual hobbies—no, that's not right either. Obviously, it's to avoid tipping anyone off.
You need to understand your enemy.

steps.speaker: Option
options: So, our genius high schooler actually studied here?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: I did RESEARCH here. They especially appointed yours truly here as a genius researcher. I'm kinda a big deal, thank you very much.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Right, right.
For sure, for sure.
Wow...

steps.content: You nod along with exaggerated eagerness, then drop your voice to a hushed, conspiratorial whisper.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then the genius researcher must know this place inside out. Probably familiar with all kinds of classified tech too, yes?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Does it have anything to do with BR-003?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Oh! Now you're speaking my language! My research field is absolutely insane, like, G*nd*m-level insane—

Your question instantly fires Summer up. Her eyes gleam, her arms flailing as words spill from her lips in a rapid-fire torrent. For someone who suffered so badly from the leak years ago, her grasp of operational security is shockingly lax.
Not that you mind.

This is round three of her theoretical lecture series. This time, though, you've done your homework. You bought the United University Ring Research Institute curriculum and study materials, diligently reading them for thirty minutes each night as an infallible sleeping pill. One month in, you're bound to understand at least a sentence or two—

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: According to established laws, energy and matter are two forms, mutually convertible. After the Perishing Star descended, a third form emerged: Mania, or you could call it psyche. Inside a Black Ring, it naturally connects to energy, and under extreme conditions, it can even convert to matter. I studied this and derived several equation sets, blah blah blah blah blah—
...Some battles aren't worth fighting. You pivot to a different topic.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So the most powerful person at the Ring Research Institute, that Director. What do you know about her?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Hmm... who?

steps.speaker: Option
options: <color=#fb9259>Isomer</color>... if I remember correctly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She's the one who should've handed you your degree at graduation. You two must have met. Ah—
You forgot she didn't graduate in the usual way.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Pfft. Graduation? A degree? A genius doesn't need any of that to prove herself. They're the ones who need to hand me titles just to prove they matter.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Borrowing lines from the T*A memes again, huh?
Wasn't attending a high school graduation your second dream?

steps.content: She flashes you another one of those wonderfully weird, utterly unclassifiable looks.
Jump

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: That's a high school graduation! Sacred, colorful youth! A place like this doesn't even come close!
end

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: I didn't come here to study anyway. I came for cutting-edge research. But the people here were so boring. We're just not on the same wavelength, and they couldn't keep up with my train of thought either. There's a wall between genius and the ordinary...
Her gaze darkens, just for a moment.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Those people didn't even get G*nd*ms! No way I'm remembering their names! Hmph.
...So what exactly is your role here? My tour guide?
You keep the words locked behind your teeth. Asking about EDGE-07 had been on your mental checklist, but it's painfully obvious she might not know a thing.
While you muse, she's already steered you to a door that whispers money and discretion. Beep, she taps her card. For all her quirks, a genius can be remarkably useful in moments like these.
The door parts, and a senior researcher from the hallowed institute sweeps forward with immaculate, eager hospitality.

steps.speaker: Research Assistant
steps.content: Are you here for the symposium? Right this way, please.
Pixel Update 5

Pixel:
Oh! And let's not forget the research projects. They're absolutely scorching hot commodities! City council, Nirvana, FAC... they all line up like good little puppies giving out business cards. Letters of intent flutter around like confetti at a parade. But hmm... something feels a little... diluted compared to a few years back.

Pixel:
Ohhh, I've got it! That so-called "academic atmosphere" has gone right out the window! Haha... Ivory tower? PLEASE. That thing never existed. Our United University students are pillars of society! Like holing up doing pure research can be more important than getting out there rubbing elbows and climbing ladders.

jsijfopg:
What's your rate for custom Hypercube field "materials"? Rush job. Money's not a problem, as long as it clears review.

Pixel:
Oho! I can practically smell another United University VIP! Tell you what, three hours from this very moment, you'll have the full package. Complete thesis, data logs, even your defense presentation slides, all gift-wrapped and ready. Since you're asking for lightspeed delivery, though, that'll be six figures to start, honey.

Pixel:
If that sounds a-okay to you, go ahead and click that link in your DMs and drop the deposit! <color=#fb9259>Academic problems? Pixel's got you covered!</color>

The venue isn't entirely unfamiliar. At first glance, it wears the air of an ivory tower, but the details tell another story: luxurious renovations, exquisite furnishings—everything is visibly expensive. Soft music and drifting fragrance fill the space, and for a moment, you're back at one of those high-society galas in Eastside, working the room for your missions.
The difference, such as it is, lies in the introductions swirling around you. They're far more intellectually demanding, adding a novel twist to an otherwise familiar scene.

steps.speaker: Research Assistant
steps.content: We have quite a few projects in today's lineup. That includes but isn't limited to Aurum Secretum tech and Apostle of Ashes correlation breakdown, BR-005 novel Mania field reconstruction and causal analysis, a preliminary look at multi-Black Ring synchronization effects, among others.

steps.speaker: Research Assistant
steps.content: Among the applied fields, next-generation autonomous mining technology has become a major focus. The breakthrough was largely enabled by the cache of Aurum Secretum weapons seized during the last campaign, and Nirvana has invested heavily in the research ever since.

steps.speaker: Research Assistant
steps.content: Oh, and of course, our conventional anti-Mania technologies. Shielding, interdiction, purification, and all the related projects. Those are making steady progress as well, with fairly mature investment channels already in place. More specifically...
The research assistant continues her enthusiastic introduction. You offer the right sounds at the right moments, but your focus keeps drifting. The subject is hard to track, yes, but more than that—
Your eyes keep straying to the other guests in the hall.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: I spotted a few Outland researchers over there. Are they the new government-sponsored arrivals? Is this really a good idea? The war barely ended, and we're already inviting the enemy into our top research facilities... Do they just not care about the city-state's security anymore?

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: Those grants came from Nirvana, specifically earmarked to attract talent. Security's important, sure, but right now, BR-005 mining is moving fast. We really can't afford to let the West District pull ahead. The competition between city-states is already underway, and scientists are essential assets. You've got to snap them up.

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: ...They could always poach that genius scientist from the Campbell family, no? I heard she's around the same age as those top researchers. Her sister's practically naturalized by now, isn't she? Quinn's been integrating plenty eagerly.

steps.speaker: Guest C
steps.content: Hard to say. The Campbell family's background seems questionable. The 9th Agency's got eyes on them too. Besides, if scientists really carry that much strategic weight, enough to threaten DisCity, we could always send agency operatives to take care of it. Cut it out at the root and whatnot. Then we'll have no problems, wouldn't you say?

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: Now that's going too far. The Ring Research Institute's hit a wall. Everyone's banking on Aurum Secretum to break things open. And think about it... we can't even retake the West District mine without unmanned extraction tech. Those West District thugs have had us by the throat long enough. We can't afford to wait any longer...
You frown. A hallowed hall of science seems like the last place you'd stumble upon such sordid talk. Summer, meanwhile, takes it in stride.
She pinches her nose, as if it's second nature.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Ugh... this place stinks. It's been years, but these people haven't changed a bit. Still can't tell what actually matters. I'd get more out of watching a few episodes of anime...

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Chief, don't hang around too long and let them rub off on you. Just look at them, honestly—oh!

You move with swift precision, skewering a rich piece of Black Forest chocolate and dropping it squarely onto Summer's plate. With the brewing rant effectively plugged, you turn your attention back to the assistant.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This is quite the event. So many distinguished names in attendance. I imagine the academic speakers will be of similar caliber, considering the Director herself is leading this too. Or so I've heard.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Will she be attending in person?

steps.speaker: Research Assistant
steps.content: You mean Director Isomer? Well... she rarely makes appearances at events like this. Her projects keep her extremely busy, and she has a great deal to manage.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Is that so? I'd heard the Director places great importance on maintaining external ties, actively building her influence. Did I have that wrong?

steps.speaker: Research Assistant
steps.content: No, no, you're quite right. It's just... headquarters has been under considerable strain recently. Every project is working against a tight schedule, and the Director is focusing on matters of greater importance.
So BR-003 really is keeping her hands full. You file the thought away and press on with your questions.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Would I have a chance to visit her, then?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm quite interested in Black Ring-related projects myself.
The research assistant hesitates, her expression betraying a flicker of reluctance.

steps.speaker: Research Assistant
steps.content: If that's what you're looking for, I'd recommend Professor Lambert's presentation. He's every bit the expert—a distinguished scholar, a respected academic leader, and Director Isomer's former advisor. Whatever questions or interests you may have, he'll be able to help.

steps.speaker: Research Assistant
steps.content: Ah, there he is, right over there. He's giving a presentation at the moment.
On the stage stands an elderly man, a professor, supposedly, in the prime of his career. Now though, he appears strikingly aged, exhaustion carved into every feature.

steps.speaker: Lambert
steps.content: ...The previous generation of unmanned mining technology relied on active Black Rings and super-loop communication. Mania data was received through dedicated channels for observation, filtering, analysis, and response.

steps.speaker: Lambert
steps.content: However, following the successive shutdown of BR-001 and BR-002, super-loop communication accuracy declined sharply. Unmanned mining malfunctions became frequent, and we were eventually forced to abandon the technology, reverting instead to the West District's more traditional—

A throat clears, interrupting the old professor mid-sentence. Someone steps up to the podium, passes him two folders, and casts a meaningful look across the room, a silent nudge to observe the investors' darkening faces.
The professor's hands begin to shake. He sets aside his prepared remarks and picks up the second file with unsteady fingers.

steps.speaker: Lambert
steps.content: ...Despite the many difficulties, we have achieved a breakthrough. A significant one. Right here, in the Ring Research Institute's most advanced field: Mania dimensional calculation.

steps.speaker: Lambert
steps.content: Our research has uncovered multiple entangled dimensions. Through separation operations, we can create dimensional fissures under experimental conditions. In time, this will undoubtedly play a major role in live combat scenarios. Many of the challenges we've faced until now can be resolved through this.

steps.speaker: Lambert
steps.content: Let's begin with the footage. After reviewing the actual case examples, we'll move on to the application with some simulated demonstrations.
He fumbles with the equipment and manages to start the footage after much difficulty. Several combat scenes begin to play.
Some of the imagery feels uncannily familiar. You take a closer look, and begin to pick out faces in the frame—

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Ooh! These scenes look kinda familiar... Wait, is this MBCC field operation footage? Chief, you're famous! You made it into a textbook case study!

steps.speaker: Option
options: Something tells me this isn't meant as a compliment.

steps.content: The recording plays on. Scene after scene, it's nothing but your failures and setbacks. From an outsider's vantage point, the whole thing comes off as almost pitiful.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: ...Hold on. Why are they only showing the parts where we get wrecked? This is slander! They're making us look bad! I oughta go over there and—mmmph mmm... Mm, delicious...
You casually shove another brownie into her open mouth, silencing her outrage while also cheering her right up.

You don't read this as personal. The wealthy just enjoy a good spectacle of misfortune, and your number came up. Though, to be fair, unearthing this handful of blunders from MBCC's sprawling archive of victories must've been quite the laborious task for the professor. It's almost impressive.
There's really no need to take such an obvious bait. Still... a quiet scoff feels warranted.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Their data's practically fossils.
This tech's got a long way to go before it sees real action.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: They're completely out of touch with actual field combat. Honestly, I'm embarrassed for them.
Jump

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Guess nothing beats frontline experience after all.
One look at Summer is all it takes. She reads you perfectly and flashes a wicked grin.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Hehe... How about we give them a live demo then?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Let's show them what real cutting-edge, frontline anti-Mania combat strategy looks like under the command of the MBCC Chief.

Her smirk sharpens, hand poised above her mini terminal. You spot a line of mischief waiting on the display, coiled and ready. One glance and you already know—the genius girl has thrown herself into the part entirely.

options: Why not?
Well, not like I could stop you anyway.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Let's contribute to the academic discourse, then.
